Data Storage & External Services

Both web workload manifests configure a connection to the Service Fabric DNS name eshopmodernized.sqldata on TCP 1433 and name the Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb database. A separate SQL application package declares the SQL Server container. No other external service integration is established by the scoped deployment files.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC and Web Forms workloads are separate stateless Service Fabric applications and container packages.
  • Both workloads are configured to target the SQL container by Service Fabric DNS; actual application-level database behavior is not visible here.
  • The web application manifests declare singleton partitions and default instance counts of -1; the SQL application parameters set one instance.

Communication Patterns

The Service Fabric application manifests configure client-facing HTTP ports 5115 (MVC) and 5114 (Web Forms), each mapped to container port 80. Both web service manifests configure an SQL connection to the eshopmodernized.sqldata DNS name on port 1433. The application code is not present, so the actual call pattern, retry/timeout behavior, service discovery implementation, response composition, and API authorization cannot be verified. TLS and authentication are not declared in the inspected service manifests.

Primary Workflows

Deployment connectivity

The application manifests declare independent stateless MVC and Web Forms services. Each service receives a database connection setting for the SQL service at eshopmodernized.sqldata:1433; the manifests do not show application queries, user actions, business rules, or readiness gating. No end-to-end business workflow can be reconstructed from these deployment assets.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The only declared cross-service data path is from the MVC and Web Forms containers to the SQL DNS name and catalog database identified in their connection settings. The deployment descriptors do not reveal which entities or operations cross this boundary, nor do they specify fallback behavior if SQL is unavailable.
